correctness.rationale: Condition on the unordered first-i value set. Prefix and suffix orderings are conditionally independent, and the prefix record has conditional probability 1/i. For i<j the inverse record either is impossible or depends only on the suffix and the set; inversion handles i>j. On the diagonal the only nonzero conditional covariance occurs when the prefix value set equals [i], an event of probability 1/binom(n,i); then both indicators coincide with the event that position i contains value i, yielding variance (i-1)/i^2. Total covariance and asymptotic correlation follow from summation and independent initial ranks. The exact finite script passed 292 assertions through n=9; the proof, not enumeration, establishes all n.

value.rationale: Both the chronological and value-ordered record processes are canonical permutation statistics. The theorem classifies every pair of their local events and identifies a sharp all-n exception at matching indices, with a concrete prefix-set mechanism. A diagonal cross-covariance structure is stronger and more structural than a marginal expectation or arbitrarily selected small case; it clarifies how two global-order encodings couple locally.
